Community types

Source: R/community_types.r
ecodive_types.Rd

enterotype() (and the planned valencia() and dmm()) assign each sample to one of a few community types, and return a data frame of class c("ecodive_<method>", "ecodive_types", "data.frame"), with one row per sample, in the input's order, and the sample names as row names.

Columns

  • sample: the sample's name (or its position, for unnamed samples).

  • type: the type assigned to it, a factor whose levels ("1", "2", ...) are the types in order.

  • Columns of the method: for enterotype(), silhouette, the sample's silhouette width.

Attributes

  • types: a data frame, one row per type: type, n_samples, top_feature (the feature of largest mean proportion, Arumugam et al.'s "driver"; NA without abundances), and columns of the method, such as enterotype()'s medoid and silhouette.

  • profiles: a types \(\times\) features matrix of each type's mean proportions (NULL without abundances).

  • selection: a data frame, one row per number of types tried, with the criterion that chose among them, and selected, TRUE for the one chosen.

  • method: the function that made the result, such as "enterotype".

Using the types

res$type is a plain factor, so it can be given as groups to any test, such as permanova(), or to an ordination's plot(), to colour the samples by type.

See also

enterotype(), plot.ecodive_types()

Examples

    et <- enterotype(iris[, 1:4], n_types = 2:5)
    et
#> # Enterotypes of Jensen-Shannon Distance
#> # 150 samples in 2 types, chosen by the Calinski-Harabasz index from 2 to 5
#> #
#> # Types:
#>   type n_samples top_feature  medoid silhouette
#> 1 1           50 Sepal.Length 39          0.825
#> 2 2          100 Sepal.Length 78          0.821
#> #
#> # Selection:
#>   n_types   ch silhouette objective selected
#> 1       2 2000      0.822    0.0268     TRUE
#> 2       3 1630      0.565    0.0208    FALSE
#> 3       4 1310      0.549    0.0191    FALSE
#> 4       5  988      0.405    0.0175    FALSE
#> #
#> # Samples: a data.frame: 150 × 3
#>    sample type  silhouette
#>    <chr>  <fct>      <dbl>
#> 1  1      1          0.877
#> 2  2      1          0.85
#> 3  3      1          0.88
#> 4  4      1          0.855
#> 5  5      1          0.871
#> 6  6      1          0.808
#> 7  7      1          0.836
#> 8  8      1          0.877
#> 9  9      1          0.858
#> 10 10     1          0.795
#> # … 140 more rows
#> # Use print(x, n = ...) to see more rows
#> # Attributes: types, profiles, selection, objective, ch, method
    table(et$type)
#> 
#>   1   2 
#>  50 100 
    attr(et, 'types')
#>   type n_samples  top_feature medoid silhouette
#> 1    1        50 Sepal.Length     39  0.8245819
#> 2    2       100 Sepal.Length     78  0.8207907
    attr(et, 'selection')
#>   n_types        ch silhouette  objective selected
#> 1       2 2000.8520  0.8220544 0.02681756     TRUE
#> 2       3 1630.9986  0.5647328 0.02078605    FALSE
#> 3       4 1311.9767  0.5491302 0.01906313    FALSE
#> 4       5  988.3541  0.4046429 0.01748311    FALSE

    # The types as groups.
    permanova(jensen(iris[, 1:4]), et$type)
#> Permutational multivariate analysis of variance (PERMANOVA) of Jensen-Shannon Distance
#> 
#> F =  1724, p = 0.001, z =  1274
#> Permutations: 999 (free)
#> 
#> Model R2 = 0.921. Model tested as a whole:
#> 
#>           Df SumOfSqs    R2    F Pr(>F)    
#> Model      1   1.4481 0.921 1724  0.001 ***
#> Residual 148   0.1243 0.079                
#> Total    149   1.5724 1.000                
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
